metadata.name: Red LED - 5mm
metadata.description: A generic red LED (~1.8V forward voltage, 633nm wavelength)
metadata.author: Brendan Howell

cathode.name: cathode
cathode.description: cathode pin (negative, shorter leg, flat side of lens)

connectionGuide.purpose: The cathode connects to ground (GND) to complete the LED circuit. Current flows from anode through the LED to cathode, then to ground.
warnings: Must connect to ground - LED will not light if polarity is reversed
Never connect cathode directly to a positive voltage source
troubleshooting: If LED doesn't light, check that cathode is connected to GND
The cathode is the SHORTER leg and has a flat edge on the LED housing
Try swapping the LED orientation if it doesn't light

connectionGuide.purpose: The anode receives current from the GPIO pin (through a current-limiting resistor). This is where power enters the LED to make it light up.
warnings: ALWAYS use a current-limiting resistor (typically 220Ω) between GPIO and anode
Direct connection to GPIO without resistor will damage the LED and possibly the Pico
The Pico's GPIO pins output 3.3V - too much current without a resistor
troubleshooting: If LED doesn't light: verify GPIO pin is set to OUTPUT in your code
If LED is dim: check resistor value - lower resistance = brighter (but more current)
If LED burns out quickly: resistor value is too low or missing
The anode is the LONGER leg of the LED

warnings: LED requires current-limiting resistor in series
Anode voltage must be higher than cathode voltage
Typical operating current is 10mA for good brightness and longevity
Connect anode to signal/power, cathode to ground
